articles.headline: Where to find the giant crab safe code and Crabshack VF5 SMG in GTA 6
keyFacts: Polygon reported that Grand Theft Auto 6 features an optional event called Pelican Valley Outpost where players can find a giant crab and the Crabshack VF5 SMG.
Polygon stated that players can locate the safe code by investigating a research facility on an island southwest of the Pelican Valley label.
Polygon explained that players can unlock the boathouse using an emergency protocol code found inside the safe to claim the weapon.
body: Grand Theft Auto 6 has a giant crab haunting the swamps and, more importantly, the Crabshack VF5 SMG, a crab-themed gun, to help your future career prospects. It's all part of an optional event called Pelican Valley Outpost that sees you pick up the pieces of some questionable experiments carried out on behalf of a store chain. It's worth the trouble, even aside from the standout weapon. There's some cash to help reach your next family fund milestone and a free jet ski, too. Best of all, this little excursion is completely safe, assuming you don't run afoul of the local gator population.
Below, we show you where to find the giant crab in GTA 6 so you can clear the Pelican Valley Outpost and get the Crabshack VF5 SMG.
Where to find the giant crab safe code in GTA 6

Pelican Valley Outpost, where the giant crab research facility is, has several codes you need to find on your way to getting the standout weapon. You'll find it on a medium-sized island southwest of the "Pelican Valley" name label on the map. Once you remove the fog from the region map, you can see it's one of the only islands in the area with buildings on it.

Take Jason's boat from his house, and set out. Definitely don't swim here, even if you're already nearby. There are too many gators for this to be a safe option. You can dock your boat at the boathouse and follow the jetty to the research facility proper. The boathouse is locked, but you'll get inside before leaving.

You'll see several buildings in the compound, but if you venture inside the first shack, you'll notice the power is off. You can still explore it, though you can't access the researcher's computer, which is essential for clearing the outpost. Head outside and around the back of the building near the blue crab cages. Interact with the breaker box to turn the power on, and head back inside. Ignore the computer for now, and take a right. There's a bag of chips in the kitchen if you want Jason to pack on some calories, and the login password for the computer is in the small bedroom opposite the kitchen. Investigate the small piece of wood on the floor to see all the choices, with "CLEAVES" being the most recent.

Interact with the computer, and press left on the direction pad to enter CLEAVES. You can skim through a few tabs of information on-screen, but the important one is the note in the green cell that says "Safe code = Double Success." Leave when you're finished.
Karkinos, the giant crab from the report, will jump you in a short cutscene, but you don't have to fight her. Press the on-screen button to push her off, and she'll vanish into the swamp.

If you want to get the giant crab safe code yourself, head to the research lab behind the shack next. There's a table with a trauma kit and some Zombix inside, which is handy, and in the specimen room you'll find Karkinos' former home and a list of experiments. Only one was a success, number 36. The code, "double success," refers to doubling the number of the successful experiment, making the code 0072.
Go back into the shack, and enter 0072 on the safe. Inside, you'll find a stack of money ($1,107 for us) and another note that reads "Emergency go protocol: 0212."
How to get the Crabshack VF5 SMG in GTA 6

The emergency protocol is the boathouse code. Leave the research compound, return to the boathouse, and input 0212 on the keypad. The door will open. Karkinos' caretaker wasn't as lucky as Jason, but their loss is your gain. Pick up the Crabshack VF5 SMG from their corpse, and you can grab a bag of marked bills to drop off at Brian's lockup later, too.
You can leave the compound the way you came, or you can hop on the jet ski and make your way home that way.

If you're just getting started in GTA 6, we have plenty of guides to help you live the high life in Leonida. Check out our GTA 6 beginner guide to get a grasp of the basics and our tips for what to do first, recommendations for the best ways to make money fast, and an explainer for how to keep stolen weapons and cars to make the most of your free time.

Our selection of GTA 6 guides includes help for things like how to steal the Phoenix in "Unwanted Attention" and whether you should defuse Mandy, too. There's a set of explainers for GTA 6's more open-ended side activities, like how to rob the Exotic Animal Front and where to find tree effigies for the Skunk Ape mission, and we've got all the GTA 6 cheat codes. You'll have to put in some effort before you can use those, though.

articles.headline: Brady Hart gets start as Texas A&M makes change at quarterback for Oklahoma game
keyFacts: Texas A&M coach Mike Elko started sophomore quarterback Brady Hart against Oklahoma on Saturday, replacing Marcel Reed.
The quarterback change followed consistent offensive struggles and a 22-7 loss to Tennessee the previous week.
The team needed to win its final two games to secure bowl eligibility.
body: Brady Hart got his first start for Texas A&M on Saturday at Oklahoma, replacing an ineffective Marcel Reed in the Aggies' next-to-last game of the regular season. (Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)
NORMAN, Okla. - Mike Elko has opted for a change in quarterback for Texas A& M 's final road game of a disappointing 2026 season.
Brady Hart's first career start Saturday against Oklahoma comes one week after he received his most meaningful playing time of the season.

The sophomore quarterback entered the Aggies' 22-7 loss to Tennessee last week with under 3 minutes remaining and completed two of his three pass attempts for 22 yards before throwing an interception. Following the consistent struggles of returning starter Marcel Reed, Hart's entry received a standing ovation by fans at Kyle Field.
A week later, Hart was handed the offense from the opening snap against an Oklahoma (6-4) defense which ranks fifth in the SEC in yards allowed (294.6).

Hart had appeared in four games this season for the Aggies (4-6), completing 14 of 24 passes for 165 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. His most productive outing came in A&M's blowout win over The Citadel , when Hart completed 8 of 12 passes for 107 yards and a touchdown. He also had two carries for 8 yards.

Saturday's change came after an increasingly rough stretch for an Aggie offense that entered the OU matchup ranked 13th in the SEC in total offense (341.2). A&M managed just 179 yards against Tennessee, never reached the red zone and scored seven points. Reed completed nine of 22 passes for 71 yards and an interception before Hart was put in the game.
Elko took responsibility for the offense after the loss, calling it "inept" and "completely non-functional" while pushing back against the idea that the problems could be attributed solely to Reed.
The opportunity in Norman put Hart in the middle of the Aggies' final push for bowl eligibility, needing to win their final two games in order to receive an invitation.

articles.headline: Wilton field hockey scores with 52 seconds left to beat Branford for first CIAC title since 2015
keyFacts: Casey O'Connor scored the winning goal with 52 seconds left to give Wilton a 1-0 victory against Branford in the CIAC Class M final.
This victory marks Wilton's seventh CIAC title and its first since 2015.
Branford coach Peter Frye said it was unfortunate the late goal did not give his team a chance to respond.
body: Casey O'Connor, center, of Wilton and her teammates celebrate their 1-0 victory against Branford in the CIAC Class M Field Hockey Championship in Wethersfield on November 10, 2026. O'Connor scored the winning goal. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media)

WETHERSFIELD - Wilton field hockey player Maeve Ryder had barely gotten her cleat back on when the ball found her stick. She immediately sent in a hard cross, and Casey O'Connor was waiting to tip it over the goalie's head with 52 seconds left to play, giving No. 2 Wilton its first CIAC title in over a decade with a 1-0 win over No. 1 Branford on Saturday in the Class M final at Wethersfield High School.
It is Wilton's seventh CIAC title but its first since 2015.

O'Connor had just been released from a penalty and got herself in position to flick in the game-winning goal, while Ryder lost her shoe in a collision and had just pounded her foot back into it when she got the ball.

"I came right off the penalty box and I knew we had less than a minute left and I knew we had to do this and end it because I was too tired to play 7 vs. 7," O'Connor said. "I stuck my stick out in front and I saw it going up. When it went in, I was ecstatic. It was so much fun."
Wilton coach Leon Kerr said the play developed just as they practiced it, other than Ryder's shoe coming off.

"We have been working on that with a packed circle and trying to put two forwards in there and getting the ball across and get a stick on it," Kerr said. "Once you get a stick on a hard pass, it will pop and we know that this goalie likes to go flat, so we worked on trying to pop the ball over her."
O'Connor is one of 12 seniors on the Wilton team, making this run to a championship even more special.
"This means the world," O'Connor said. "We have worked for this, and the coaches have done such a great job preparing us. It was a collective effort and everyone did their part."
Wilton controlled much of the game, though Ellie Meyran of Branford broke out for several scoring chances without converting.
Branford was playing in its third straight Class M title game and was the defending champion.

"We have been resilient all season and it was unfortunate that goal came so late because it didn't give us a chance to respond," Branford coach Peter Frye said. "We knew this was going to be a really tight game and expected a one-goal game."
Branford was playing in its 18th championship game, while Wilton was making its 12th trip to a final.
Player of the Game
Casey O'Connor, Wilton : The senior won the regular-season game between the two teams with an overtime goal and was in position to win this one and deliver a state title in the process.

"This means a lot. We have 12 seniors and they have been playing together since grade six. This is a culmination of all that work from sixth grade up to today."

articles.headline: ‘GO NAVY’ becomes ‘GO ARMY’ after overnight prank at Navy football stadium
keyFacts: Security footage showed uniformed Army cadets rearranged bolted seat backs at the Naval Academy stadium overnight to change GO NAVY to GO ARMY.
Stadium workers restored the original seating message before kickoff and Navy did not expect any legal repercussions from the rivalry prank.
Navy will face Army on 12 December in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
body: The large letters that spell “GO NAVY” in the upper seating level of the Naval Academy’s football stadium were changed to “GO ARMY” in an elaborate overnight prank before the Midshipmen hosted No 24 Memphis on Saturday.

The stunt involved rearranging the blue and yellow seat backs at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium in Annapolis, Maryland, a task made considerably more complicated by the fact that the seats are bolted into place.
The letters were back to normal well before the noon kickoff. A Navy spokesperson said security footage showed uniformed Army cadets in the stadium between 1am and 4am.

According to the Athletic, stadium workers began restoring the original message at 6am, completing the job before the gates opened to spectators four hours later. Navy reportedly regarded the operation as a successful rivalry prank and did not expect any legal repercussions.

A member of ESPN’s TV broadcast team posted a picture on social media at 10.19am with the explanation: “Not AI ... 20 staff members have been working for the last couple of hours to fix the seat backs. Army Navy rivalry heating up already.”

The stunt was the latest chapter in a decades-long tradition of elaborate practical jokes between the two military academies, known as “spirit missions”, which have frequently involved the theft of each other’s mascots.

In 1991, Navy midshipmen made off with four of Army’s mule mascots, while Army cadets have repeatedly targeted Navy’s goat, Bill. A 2021 raid famously resulted in the wrong goat being taken. The academies signed an agreement in 1992 intended to put an end to mascot thefts, although the tradition has proved difficult to stamp out.
In 2022, Navy personnel flew three small aircraft over the West Point campus, scattering ping-pong balls bearing pro-Navy slogans along with leaflets.
The overnight incursion did little to spoil Navy’s Saturday. The Midshipmen upset Memphis 38-34, improving to 4-6 after entering the game with just three victories in nine outings.
Navy face Army on 12 December in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

articles.headline: Comcast: 'At peak, GTA 6 accounted for nearly a quarter of all internet traffic'
keyFacts: Comcast stated that the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 caused the biggest internet traffic day in its network history.
Comcast reported that network traffic climbed 31 percent above average, with the game accounting for nearly a quarter of all network traffic at its peak.
Comcast shared a graph illustrating the traffic spike on November 19, though the data only reflects Comcast's network rather than the entire internet.
body: In a post to X, "The Everything App," US entertainment and communications conglomerate Comcast revealed that Grand Theft Auto 6's historic launch drove record-breaking internet traffic. According to Comcast, only a quarter of "the entire internet" was downloading Rockstar's latest cozy game phenomenon.

"GTA 6 didn't just break records in gaming," Comcast wrote. "Its launch drove the biggest internet traffic day in our network history, with traffic climbing 31% above an average day. At peak, GTA 6 accounted for nearly a quarter of all network traffic."

Comcast shared a video of a line graph showing the massive relative spike in activity on November 19. The chart is unlabeled except for the date, but it presumably corresponds to the volume of data being downloaded across Comcast's entire network.

And that last but does add a caveat to the numbers Comcast cited: Its network and "the entire internet" are two different things, unless I'm missing something here or Comcast's data accounts for other ISPs and other countries, not just its own services.

Regardless, it's still a significant bit of fun with statistics, another example of the totalizing footprint of what may be the largest commercial launch in entertainment history. Imagine how much bigger it would have been launching on PC as well.

articles.headline: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
keyFacts: Signal is restricting screenshot capabilities on Android and iOS to prevent operating system AI from scanning screen data.
Signal President Meredith Whittaker called screen-scanning AI agents an existential threat to the app's ability to guarantee privacy.
Users can disable the screenshot restriction, but Whittaker noted this breaks Signal's privacy guarantees and is an incomplete solution.
body: Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI.

Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.”

“Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”
Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS.

That said, users can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would “break our privacy guarantees.” She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution, as it doesn’t “address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data.”

articles.headline: California prosecutor rips Newsom’s death row decision, citing technicality for SoCal prisoners
keyFacts: Orange County District Attorney Todd Spitzer asked the California Supreme Court to review Governor Gavin Newsom's commutations of 18 death row inmates.
Spitzer argued that Newsom granted mass clemency based on personal opposition to capital punishment rather than reviewing cases individually.
The California Supreme Court is preparing to review commutations involving inmates with multiple felony convictions, the article reported.
body: A prominent California district attorney is taking a swing at Gov. Gavin Newsom’s sweeping death row commutations — targeting 18 convicted killers from Orange County, including a notorious serial murderer and a child killer.
Orange County District Attorney Todd Spitzer filed a new request with the California Supreme Court Friday, urging justices to review Newsom’s decision to spare the 18 inmates from execution.

The latest challenge focuses on prisoners who had no prior felony convictions before the murders that landed them on death row. Unlike inmates with multiple felony convictions, their commutations do not automatically require approval from the state’s high court.
Advertisement
Of the 584 condemned inmates statewide who received Newsom’s clemency, 202 are set to have their sentences commuted without additional court approval, according to Spitzer’s office.
Spitzer argued in his filing that Newsom’s mass commutations were driven by his personal opposition to capital punishment rather than a case-by-case review of the law.
The governor effectively acted because he “disagrees with the law,” Spitzer argued, noting that California voters have twice rejected ballot measures to abolish the death penalty.
Advertisement

“Our criminal justice system does not bend with the political winds, and one man – even if he is the governor – does not get to put his thumb on the scales of justice simply because he does not like the law,” Spitzer said in a statement.
“I refuse to allow one man to dismantle our criminal justice system brick by brick and sentence by sentence until there is not a shred of accountability left.”
Spitzer also accused Newsom of failing to “faithfully execute” the law by granting sweeping clemency instead of evaluating the inmates’ cases individually.
Advertisement

The 18 prisoners who were sentenced to death in the county without having prior felonies are Maria del Rosio Alfaro, Ika Amulu, Alejandro Avila, Eric Wayne Bennett, Richard Delmer Boyer, Shaun Kareem Burney, Edward Charles III, Richard Lucio DeHoyos, John Joseph Famalaro, Randy Steven Kraft, Waymon Livingston, Victor Mirando Miranda-Guerrero, Christian Antonio Monterroso, Iftekhar Murtaza, Tanya Jaime Nelson, Ignacio Arriola Tafoya, Eduardo David Vargas and Daniel Patrick Wozniak.
For example, Bennett was sentenced to death in 1997 for the 1994 rape and murder of 50-year-old Marie Evans Powell.
Advertisement

Bennett— who had installed flooring or carpet at Powell’s Laguna Hills townhouse two weeks earlier— burglarized her home, raped her and fatally bludgeoned her. He was also convicted of raping and robbing another woman at knifepoint in Costa Mesa.

Kraft is a notorious serial killer who committed the rape, torture and murder of a minimum of sixteen young men across Southern California between 1972 and 1983. Investigators have also linked him or suspected him in dozens of additional killings, with estimates ranging up to 67 total victims across three states.

Avila is a convicted murderer who kidnapped, sexually assaulted, and killed 5-year-old Samantha Runnion in Stanton, California, in 2002. Avila abducted the child while she was playing outside her home. Her body was found the following day about 50 miles away in Riverside County.
Advertisement
But the latest legal challenge could face questions over whether the state’s constitution gives Newsom clear authority to commute the sentences of inmates with no prior felony convictions.

Attorney Scott Sanders, who represents Wozniak, questioned the purpose of Spitzer’s filing, telling City News Service: “I’m not exactly sure what the goal is in filing the brief. The law appears to be completely settled on this issue in terms of a governor’s right to commute.”
Newsom has defended his sweeping decision as a matter of conscience, arguing that he was morally compelled to spare the condemned inmates.
“But the constitution also gave every governor clemency authority, and that power exists for moments when law as applied cannot be squared with justice. For me, this is that moment,” Newsom wrote.
Victim advocacy groups have separately taken their objections to the state Supreme Court as it prepares to review commutations involving inmates with multiple felony convictions.

Crime Victims United on Friday asked Associate Justice Kelli Evans to recuse herself from that process, because she formerly worked for Newsom and reportedly helped create his 2019 executive order placing a moratorium on executions, which is still in place.
The justice swiftly denied that request, prompting outcry from advocates for an explanation. The Post reached out to the state supreme court for comment.

articles.headline: New Report Claims Jensen Huang Regularly Threatened Nvidia Staff With Over-The-Top Violence
keyFacts: Former Nvidia staff told the New York Times that CEO Jensen Huang routinely made violent threats and verbally abused employees.
A spokesperson for Huang claimed the allegations are fabrications, citing ongoing support from numerous Nvidia staff members.
Huang recently resigned following an internal investigation, and investors are reportedly rattled by the leadership shake-up.
body: The past few weeks for Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang have been high stakes and humiliating. After confirming an affair with a possible spy, the chip maker announced their own internal investigation into Huangâs behavior. Ever since, new infidelities have emerged and Huang announced his resignation. According to a new report from the New York Times, the humiliation might be karmic, as former Nvidia staff say the CEO routinely sought to make examples of employees with outlandish, violent threats.

In behavior more fitting for Yosemite Sam, Nvidia staff tell the Times that Huang maintained a culture of verbal abuse. Staff say Huang threatened those around him with dismemberment, ripping off employees arms, beating them to death with them, and peeing into their brain. The Times says one executive was told that his mother should have considered abortion. It seems he believed this kind of harassment was good for oneâs resolve, previously telling Stripe CEO Patrick Collison that “Iâd rather torture you into greatness, because I believe in you.”

At the heart of the AI boom, Nvidia has become one of the most influential companies in the world. While the pressure did seem to intensify Haungâs hostility, the attitude is hardly new. On top of anonymous statements, the Times spoke with former human resources VP Michael Winston and company lawyer Stephen Pettigrew, who both filed lawsuits over company culture in 2005 and 2007 respectively. The paper was provided with legal documents.

A statement from Huangâs spokesperson claims these new allegations are “fabrications that are now impossible to disprove specifically,” citing the number of Nvidia staff who continue to support Huang as evidence of good leadership.

Few things about this scandal have been clean for Nvidia or the AI industry at large. Days after his resignation, Huang has already expressed interest in returning to his post, though the companyâs board seems to feel differently. One of the prime drivers and biggest benefactors to the AI explosion, investors seem rattled at the companyâs shake up, especially after the ‘Blue Wave’ ushered in a class of lawmakers intent on introducing policy around the tech and slowing down data centers. articles.headline: How long can fiber optic cables be before they lose signal?
keyFacts: Fiber optic cables transmit data using light through glass strands, offering faster connections than copper lines.
Uninterrupted single fiber strands typically span several kilometers before signal strength weakens due to attenuation.
Transcontinental fiber cable systems use optical amplifiers installed along the seabed to boost signals over long distances.
body: How long can fiber optic cables be before they lose signal?
Pretty long, it turns out.

Fiber optic cables are responsible for a significant portion of the world's Internet infrastructure. You may know that the technology is responsible for carrying data signals across oceans, but fiber has also become increasingly common in our cities and even homes. Many internet service providers (ISPs) use fiber-optic as a selling point, and for good reason: It offers a significant internet speed upgrade over legacy DSL connections that rely on copper telephone lines.

The longest fiber optic cable run in the world is the 2Africa cable system. It's an underwater optical fiber cable that has landing points in many African countries as well as Europe and Asia. The previous record was held by SEA-ME-WE 3, a cable system that connected portions of Europe, Northern Africa, the Middle East, Asia, and Australia. That system was decommissioned in 2024.
As with any technology, fiber-optic cables have their limits. So how long can a fiber-optic cable actually be before signal loss makes the data being transmitted completely unrecoverable?
How do fiber optic cables carry data over long distances?

Fiber-optic cables rely on a physics principle called total internal reflection to transmit data through glass (or sometimes plastic) strands in the form of light. The glass core has a high enough refractive index so that when light hits the boundary at a sufficiently shallow angle, it reflects back into the core rather than passing through. This allows the light to travel long distances without experiencing significant energy loss or signal deterioration.

This is in stark contrast to Ethernet cables, which rely on twisted pairs of copper wires to transmit data in the form of electrical current. Like any metallic conductor, copper wires have some resistance, which means you can't use them for very long distances. The maximum recommended length for Cat5e Ethernet cables is just 100 meters or slightly over 300 feet. They're also affected by electromagnetic interference, affecting their reliability over long runs.

By comparison, fiber optic cables can carry data over several kilometers before the signal starts breaking down. A single fiber-optic cable can bundle multiple individual fibers, each capable of carrying its own data signals. This is why internet service providers advertise their use of fiber over traditional copper wiring when deploying city-wide networks. The end result is a much faster connection that's often more consistent.

However, fiber optic cables have limits too. Even with total internal reflection, a small amount of light is lost as it travels through the glass core due to absorption and scattering. This gradual reduction in signal strength is called attenuation. Over a long enough run, this weakens the signal until the receiver can no longer distinguish between useful data and noise.
How long can a single fiber-optic cable run be?

A single uninterrupted glass fiber can typically span several kilometers before signal loss becomes a limiting factor. Keep in mind, fiber-optic cables also come in two types: single-mode and multi-mode.

Single-mode fiber only allows one beam of light to travel through it at a time, while multi-mode fiber allows multiple light pulses (called modes) to propagate through the strands simultaneously. These pulses take slightly different paths within the strand, which means they can arrive at different times. This is called modal dispersion and eventually causes the receiver to struggle interpreting the data signal.

Single-mode fiber is capable of carrying signals over longer distances but requires specific equipment that can cost significantly more money. Multi-mode fiber cables have wider cores that makes optical alignment with transceiver equipment easier, so they're often the preferred choice for shorter fiber runs. With longer runs, though, single-mode fiber's stability can justify the higher equipment costs.

Regardless of the operating mode, you likely won't have to worry about signal loss in a typical home network. Even multi-mode fiber can cover hundreds of meters. The bigger problem in a domestic fiber cable run is often caused by bends that are too tight, which can cause light leakage from the core.

In the case of fiber optic systems running across continents, they use optical amplifiers to compensate for signal loss over long distances. These devices are installed along the seabed and designed to boost the optical signal. A technique known as multiplexing then allows multiple data streams to travel simultaneously over a single strand. Put simply: You never have a truly uninterrupted fiber optic cable running over such vast distances.

articles.headline: Public-access television is born anew in NIGHT EYE TV, a digital goggle box filled with art game curios
keyFacts: NIGHTEYE.TV is a new digital platform styled like public-access television that currently features clips and links to various art games.
The platform's creators plan for it to become a curated store where users can purchase a rotating selection of games.
An Indiegogo campaign is currently running to help make the platform fully operational.
body: I am both a bit too young and a bit too very not American to have ever experienced public-access television, but it's something that's always fascinated me. For those too young to have even heard of it, or just not in the know, it essentially allowed anyone to broadcast their own shows through cable TV. A proto YouTube, if you will. It's obviously not what it was any more, given the advent of the internet, but in NIGHTEYE.TV, it may be making a digital, more interactive return.

NIGHTEYE.TV is a strange little place. I call it a place, it's a fake TV floating in a Unity default texture void, lending it a Backroomsian vibe, but even if there's not much there to ground yourself in, the goggle box is enticing all the same. It beckons you to turn it on, a series of buttons all linking to different "channels." What awaits you isn't television, however. Instead you'll find games, mostly of the weirdo, freako, sicko variety, quickly setting the tone.
🌕NIGHT EYE TV’s initial form is live!🌑
Check out the site and follow our Indiegogo campaign at www.nighteye.tv!
[image or embed]
— NIGHT EYE TV (@nighteye-tv.bsky.social) October 14, 2026 at 2:05 AM

In its current incarnation, it's mostly just a collection of clips of these various art games, with direct links to them hidden away in a menu, but a good collection it is. You'll find Nathalie Lawhead's Everything is Going to Be OK, Jeremy Couillard's more recent Soul Injector Commando, and Taylor McCue's He Fucked The Girl Out Of Me. Some clips are longer than others, acting as sort of segments of playthroughs, but it all feels like an exciting evolution of what public-access television was.

The ultimate goal is for it to be a curated platform where you can buy a rotating selection of games. Most of the sale goes back to the original artist, and 15% gets put into a community pool to be split amongst all of the contributors, with the last 15% going towards keeping everything running. body: Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX) revealed he spoke with incoming Sen. James Talarico (D-TX) for “probably a half hour” over the phone on Friday about bringing the U.S. Space Academy to Texas .

Texas is one of 25 states vying to host the proposed Space Academy after President Donald Trump signed an executive order in August to create a training school for the Space Force . The Lone Star State wants to place the academy near the NASA Johnson Space Center in Houston.

NASA publicly identified 15 of the 25 states that have submitted bids for the Space Academy: Alabama, Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Indiana, Louisiana, Maryland, Nevada, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, and West Virginia.

articles.headline: Raya set to have scan on injury - how much would Arsenal miss him?
keyFacts: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya injured his shoulder during a 2-2 draw with Newcastle and will undergo an MRI scan.

body: - Published
Injuries are never good news, but Arsenal's latest one to first-choice goalkeeper David Raya has come in the worst possible position.
The 31-year-old was forced to leave the pitch 70 minutes into Saturday's 2-2 draw with Newcastle, appearing to hurt his shoulder in an innocuous challenge with Magpies forward William Osula.
The Gunners arguably have the best depth in the league with at least two quality options in all outfield positions after a period of squad strengthening.
In goal, however, cover appears much thinner.

Raya was a key component in Arsenal's Premier League title-winning campaign last season, was named in the Fifpro Men's World 11 and was unlucky to not win the Yashin Trophy, awarded to the world's best goalkeeper, which went to Spain team-mate Unai Simon.

Behind him, Kepa Arrizabalaga still holds the record as the most expensive goalkeeper in football history following his Â£72m move from Athletic Bilbao to Chelsea in August 2018, but is far behind Raya in terms of quality.
Raya's passing range and ability on the ball are key to how Arsenal build their attacks, and his presence is a big reason why they have the best defence in the league.
They have conceded just seven Premier League goals this season, with only Brighton able to match that tally - having played a game fewer.
Arsenal also brought in former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier on a free transfer in the summer but his only appearance this season came in the embarrassing Carabao Cup defeat by League Two Fleetwood.
When asked about Raya's injury, Arteta said he did not know how severe the issue is.
"Well, unfortunately, he had to come off, which is never good news," said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.
"He will get assessed now, and probably he will have an MRI [scan] tomorrow to see what it is exactly he has done.
"I don't know how it happened, and what the injury is at the moment, so we'll have to wait and see tomorrow."
'Raya the one player Arsenal can't afford to lose'
Arsenal are about to enter a gruelling period of games - with or without Raya.
In the next four weeks, they face Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid.

"The one player that Arsenal cannot afford to lose is David Raya," said former England forward Alan Shearer, who is a pundit on Saturday's BBC Match of the Day. "He has made such a difference since joining from Brentford in 2023.

"They have top-class cover in just about every other position but he is the one individual that Mikel Arteta will be thinking 'we don't want to play without him for an extended period'. They could, of course go into the transfer market if they need to in January, but Arteta will be desperately hoping Raya is not out for long."
Raya is reportedly close to agreeing a new deal at the club, which shows his importance to the Gunners with two years remaining on his contract.
Ex-England midfielder Jamie Redknapp said on Sky Sports that Raya is "irreplaceable".
"Kepa is not up to the level of him - I actually think he struggles in the Premier League," added Redknapp. "Obviously we've seen in the Carabao Cup last year in the final.
"He is now going to have to play some games and that's going to be difficult for him.

"It will change everything for Arsenal for a while so that's a massive blow depending on how long David Raya is out because he is irreplaceable - probably the best goalkeeper in the Premier League, if not one of the best in the world."

articles.headline: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
keyFacts: Mexican authorities arrested wanted drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores following a deadly shoot-out in Sinaloa, the defence secretariat said.
Meza Flores was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list for leading a cartel accused of trafficking fentanyl and other drugs.

body: - Published
A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities.
Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores and seven others were detained by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said.
Seven suspects were killed in the operation, as were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave, the secretariat added.

Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs" by the FBI. The US is seeking his extradition.
Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump since he returned to the White House.

Meza Flores, the leader of the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, is thought to have been active in the drug trafficking trade since the 1990s but managed to evade authorities till now by maintaining a relatively low profile.

Using US intelligence on his whereabouts, Mexican special forces descended on his location using "stealth and surprise", establishing a perimeter to prevent him from escaping and reinforcements arriving, Mexico's defence secretariat said.
However, they "came under attack from gunfire and explosives" before entering the property and arresting Meza Flores, the secretariat continued.
Videos circulating online appear to show helicopters firing streams of bullets towards the ground in Guasave. Others appear to show people at a baseball stadium fleeing as they hear shooting sounds.
Eight people in total were arrested, including Meza Flores' second-in-command, who is also his cousin, and his brother-in-law, who is the group's financial operator, the secretariat added.
Meza Flores, his cousin, and his brother-in-law were flown to Mexico City to face prosecution, the defence secretariat said. The other five remained in the state of Sinaloa.
Authorities also said they had seized multiple weapons during the operation, including a grenade launcher, as well as drugs and cash.
When Meza Flores was added to the FBI's most-wanted list in 2025, he was accused of "heinous crimes" including kidnapping, extortion and torture.
Then-acting FBI director Brian Driscoll said Meza Flores and his organisation had also unleashed a "scourge of illicit drugs" into the US via its southern border with Mexico.
He was initially charged with drug trafficking in the US in 2012 before being charged again in 2019.
The 44-year-old is alleged to have conspired to manufacture and distribute large quantities of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana between 2005 and 2019.

Meza Flores was originally a high-ranking member of the BeltrÃ¡n Leyva Organization, but a split between rival factions led to a surge of violence and prompted him to establish his own cartel by 2013.

His organisation has also engaged in what US officials described as an "extremely violent turf war" with the Sinaloa Cartel, one of the most powerful drug trafficking gangs, which operates in the same region.
Meza Flores was added to the FBI's most-wanted list after Mexican authorities reportedly linked his cartel to 20 million fentanyl pills they seized in 2024.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has taken a tougher stance on the country's cartels in a bid to resist US intervention on Mexican soil. Mexico has welcomed closer collaboration but resisted US boots on the ground.
Trump made stemming the flow of drugs into the US across its southern border one of his key election pledges.

articles.headline: Nearly all software teams admit to shipping AI-generated code as study finds verification 'has not kept pace with that shift'
keyFacts: A TestMu AI report found that 81% of software teams admitted to merging AI-generated code they did not fully understand.
TestMu AI CEO Asad Khan noted that verification of AI-generated code has not kept pace with the increasing volume of AI output.
Khan expects independent validation of AI output to become the standard for engineering organizations to prevent defects.
body: - The majority of software development teams have merged code with AI contributions that they didn’t understand
- Some teams (55%) manually review code, while others use one AI model to review another, which has mixed results
- TestMu AI’s State of AI in Quality Engineering 2026 report has also found that only 13% of teams have an incident response provision for publishing AI-generated errors

Generative AI coding tool shave been wholeheartedly embraced by software development teams, to such an extent that 81% have admitted to merging AI generated code that wasn’t fully understood, new research has claimed.

TestMu AI’s State of AI in Quality Engineering 2026 report also found a mixed approach to reviewing AI code and very few teams employing an incident response procedure in the event of AI generated errors occurring on live projects.

These results raise some questions on how development teams are using AI and what steps are being employed to verify output. While some teams use manual review, others rely on a second LLM to review and judge the code. However, this appears to have increased the likelihood of code no-one understands being published.
LLM-as-a-judge

Revealed in the report is the notion of the verification gap, a challenge for teams relying on AI-generated code. Just 41% of teams use automated checks of AI-written code before merging it with existing, often live code. This gap is the beginning of the problem – there is simply too much code to efficiently check.
With 55% of development teams using manual review, or passing to a dedicated QA team (51%), it’s clear that with some teams, important measures are in place.

Employing a second LLM to grade the generated code might seem like a smart move. In terms of fixing issues, it probably is. But the result of this strategy is that teams using LLM-as-a-judge are shipping code they don’t understand at a greater rate – 29%, compared with 15% who don’t use AL grading.
Verify your output
Asad Khan, the Co-founder and CEO of TestMu AI said the key point that verification of AI-generated code is not keeping pace with the volume of output.

“Software teams now rely on AI to write their code, generate their tests, and increasingly determine whether both are ready to ship,” he noted.

“Verification, however, has not kept pace with that shift. We believe any output AI produces should be validated by a system independent of the model that produced it, before it merges and every time it changes.” The development teams that have put in place the procedures to do this are doing better, it seems.
“The teams in our survey that already follow this discipline see fewer defects reach production, and we expect it to become the standard for engineering organizations shipping with AI,” Khan added.

Countries agree to ‘start discussing options’ for rules around autonomous weapons.

Before the negotiations got underway, the International Committee of the Red Cross, the guardian of the Geneva Conventions, said it was urgent for legally binding rules to be drafted within a year. That call was backed by the U.N. secretary-general and by Pope Leo.

The compromise reached was that countries would instead have two years to propose regulations. Negotiations between countries on which regulations to adopt and how to enforce them will likely drag on well beyond that. Additionally, room was left for some of those yet-to-be-adopted regulations to remain “optional.”

Humanitarian organizations and some countries see a need to urgently adopt legally binding rules as semi-autonomous weapons and drones have been responsible for a significant number of civilian deaths in conflicts around the globe, including in Ukraine, Gaza, and Sudan.
According to NPR, Russia, Israel, and the US proved to be the primary obstructions:
On day one, Russia delayed proceedings by objecting to the meeting’s agenda. Then the United States proposed a five-year window to discuss nonbinding, optional guidelines for autonomous weapons.

articles.headline: Voters want to 'move on' from the president, former Trump official claims as reason for GOP's midterm defeat
keyFacts: Former Sen. Sam Brownback claimed Democrats won the 2026 midterms because voters rejected Donald Trump's personal leadership style rather than his policies.
Brownback noted economic concerns influenced the midterms, while a Fox News poll showed 89% of voters prioritized the cost of living.
Looking ahead to the 2028 presidential election, Vice President JD Vance said he will decide whether to run in the spring.
body: Former Kansas Republican Sen. Sam Brownback, who served as an ambassador during Donald Trump's first term, blamed the president's personal leadership style for Republicans' midterm losses.

He claims the outcome of the 2026 elections — where Democrats' sweeping victories in traditional red strongholds helped them reclaim majorities in the House and Senate — was a sign of voters rejecting Trump more than rebuking his policies.

"I think the thing we're missing is that it was really targeted at President Trump. I don't think it was targeted at the policies so much," Brownback told Fox News Digital in an interview. "Pride comes before a fall and a haughty spirit before a stumble."
REPUBLICANS TURN ON TRUMP AFTER DEVASTATING MIDTERM LOSSES HAND DEMOCRATS CONTROL OF CONGRESS
The former Kansas governor argued that Republicans should not write off the midterm results as the typical losses suffered by a president’s party through history during their second term.

Brownback, who represented Kansas in the U.S. Senate from 1996 to 2011 before serving as governor from 2011 to 2018, said economic concerns, including inflation and gas prices , played a role in the election results.
He suggested voters' frustrations extended beyond the economy to Trump's approach to governing.

The Fox News Voter Poll found that 89% of voters considered the cost of living a crucial or major factor in their congressional vote, compared with 74% who said the same about the war in Iran. The findings suggest broader economic frustrations were also a major concern among voters, although the two issues may overlap and the polling does not establish which ultimately drove Republican defections.
DEMS SEIZE ON MIDTERM ROUT TO DEMAND ICE REFORM, BUT POLLS REVEAL A TWIST IN WHO PRIORITIZED IMMIGRATION

"People just saying I'm ready to move on past President Trump," Brownback said, adding that voters still appreciated the administration's efforts to secure the border but viewed interior immigration enforcement as too aggressive.
The former ambassador-at-large for international religious freedom also urged Republicans to reconsider how they communicate with voters, emphasizing the importance of humility and kindness.
"You just can't be proud. You've got to come forward humbly," Brownback said. "And I think you have to do that with the American public."
Brownback called for a more measured response to voters' concerns ahead of 2028. "We hear you, American public. We're adjusting to the message that we heard," he said.
REPUBLICANS NEED HISTORY LESSON ABOUT THEIR PARTY IF THEY WANT TO MOVE ON FROM DEFEAT
"America is great because it's good. If it ever loses its goodness, it will lose its greatness," he added. "There has to be, as I keep doubling back to, a humility and a kindness about it as well."

Both Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have been floated as potential contenders for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination , with Vance saying he plans to decide whether to launch a White House bid in the spring.
